observation.visible_scene: A white tabletop scattered with many small cube-shaped clusters of shiny metallic magnetic balls. A long diagonal bar of balls sits on the left, and a second bar is being formed on the upper right. A human hand interacts with these bars; all other small clusters remain in fixed positions.
visible_changes: Frames 1-25: a left hand grips the near (lower-left) end of the left bar. As the hand pulls, the bar elongates along its diagonal axis and its whole body shifts rightward relative to the stationary background clusters, growing from a short row of balls into a much longer bar.
Between frames 25 and 26: the left hand leaves the frame, and the now-elongated left bar stays put in the upper-left, no longer moving.

Frames 26-41: a right hand enters at the upper-right, grasps a small compact cluster, and drags it, stretching that cluster into a longer bar oriented toward the left; the held (right) end moves slightly left while the opposite end extends leftward, so the bar lengthens.
Throughout, the numerous other small cubic clusters and the white surface do not change position, indicating the camera is essentially fixed.

The left bar's growth is a continuous stretching/translation over the segment (already underway at t=0), not a sudden onset; the right bar's stretching likewise begins mid-segment with the right hand's arrival.
outside_clip_unknowns: The compact starting state of the left bar before t=0 (it is already partly stretched at the first frame).
What happens to either bar after t=2.667 s.
Whether the bars lengthen by stretching existing balls or by picking up additional balls (no separate ball source is visible).
uncertain_details: Exact hand mechanics (pure drag vs. magnetic stretch) cannot be confirmed from the frames alone.
Minor camera motion is not fully excluded, though the fixed positions of all background clusters strongly suggest a static camera.
The transition of the left hand out of frame and the right hand in between frames 25 and 26 is not captured; only their presence/absence at the ends is visible.
